segments.say: Let your body settle. Let your shoulders soften, and your hands rest wherever they are. For the next little while, you don't need anything to be interesting. You don't need to be entertained, or engaged, or challenged. You can simply rest, in a gentle, peaceful stillness. This moment is complete just as it is.

Take a slow breath in. And let it out, slowly. Again. Breathe in gently. And let it go. Notice that your breath doesn't need to wait for anything. It comes and goes, by itself, in its own rhythm. You can simply let it.

Imagine that all the waiting of the day is like a long line of people, slowly leaving a room. One by one, they walk out through the door, quietly, until the room is empty and still. The emails. The messages. The plans. The worries. All gently leaving. And the room is quiet.

Now imagine snow, falling very slowly outside a window. Each flake drifts down in its own time. None of them is in a hurry. None of them is late. They simply fall, softly, and settle. The world outside grows quieter and quieter under a soft white blanket.

Feel the weight of your body. Your feet, heavy and warm. Your legs, sinking a little deeper. Your back, fully supported. Your arms, loose and heavy. Your head, resting completely. There's nothing to hold up. Something beneath you is holding you.

If thoughts come, that's alright. Let them be like people walking past outside, on their way somewhere else. You don't need to follow them. You don't need to wait for them to finish. Just let them pass by the window, and let the street become quiet again.

There's no clock to watch tonight. Let it be turned away. There is no time to watch. No minutes to count. Just this breath. And this one. And this one. Time can move as slowly or as quickly as it likes. You don't need to keep track.

Now imagine a small fire glowing in a quiet room. The flames move slowly, softly, never quite the same. You don't need to do anything. Just watch them in your mind's eye. Soft, warm, gently moving. A kind of fascination that asks nothing of you.

Let your forehead smooth out. Let the small muscles around your eyes soften. Let your jaw loosen just a little. Let your tongue rest. Let your throat be easy. With each breath out, let a little more of the day melt away.

You don't need to wait for sleep. You don't need to chase it. Sleep is like the tide. It comes in by itself, gently, when the time is right. All you need to do is rest here, on the shore, and let it come to you.

Let's travel slowly through the body once more. Your feet, warm and heavy. Your calves, relaxed. Your knees, soft. Your thighs, sinking. Your hips, settling. Your belly, rising and falling with each breath. Your chest, soft and open.
Your shoulders, heavy. Your arms, loose. Your hands, warm and still. Your neck, easy. Your face, calm. Your whole body, resting. Breathing slowly. Safe and warm. There's nothing more you need to do.

If you'd like, picture something good that's waiting for you, somewhere in the days ahead. Something small and kind. A walk. A meal. A friend's voice. Let yourself feel a little warmth about it. And then let it rest too. It will be there when it's time. You don't need to hold it now.
The night is long and gentle. It will carry you through, hour by hour, while your body rests and your mind sorts the day quietly in the background. You can trust the night. You can let go.
Breathe in, slowly. And out. Let each breath carry you a little further from the shore of waking. A little deeper into rest. Softer. Quieter. Slower.
There's nothing to wait for. Nothing to finish. Nothing to explain. Just the soft rhythm of your breath, the warmth of your body, and the quiet of the night around you.

Imagine you're sitting in a small wooden boat on a still lake at twilight. The boat is tied to a dock, so it can't drift away. It rocks very gently, back and forth, back and forth, with the smallest movements of the water. You don't need to row. You don't need to go anywhere.

The sky above you is turning from soft purple to deep blue. One by one, the first stars appear. You don't need to count them. You don't need to wait for all of them. They'll arrive in their own time, as they always do, every single night.

The air is cool and fresh. Somewhere across the water, a bird settles into its nest for the night. The trees on the shore are dark and still. The whole world is slowing down with you. Breathing out. Letting go.

Let your breath be slow and soft. Breathe in, and feel the cool air. Breathe out, and feel your body grow a little heavier. Again. In. And out. There's no rush. The night has all the time in the world.

Every wait you had today is finished now. The lines, the messages, the minutes on the clock. They're all behind you, like the shore in the evening mist. Nothing is waiting for you right now. And you are not waiting for anything. You're simply here, resting.
Let the gentle rocking of the boat carry you. Back and forth. Slowly. Softly. Each little movement a little slower than the last. Your eyes are heavy. Your body is warm. Your mind is quiet.
Sleep is coming, like the tide, like the stars, like the evening. You don't need to call it. It knows the way. Just rest here, safe and warm, and let it find you.

Let one last gentle wave of warmth move through you. From the top of your head, down over your face, your neck, your shoulders. Down through your arms, into your hands. Down through your chest and belly, your hips, your legs, all the way to your toes. Warm. Heavy. Calm.

If any part of you is still holding on, still waiting for something, let it know that it can rest now too. Whatever it is will still be there tomorrow, if it needs to be. For tonight, it can be set down, softly, like a book on a bedside table.
Breathe in, slowly. And out. And again. Each breath a little softer. Each moment a little quieter. The boat rocks gently. The stars shine. And you are drifting, peacefully, toward sleep.
There is nothing left to wait for. Only rest. Only the quiet night, holding you gently until morning.

Imagine lying on a soft blanket in a quiet meadow on a warm summer evening. Above you, the sky is slowly turning from gold to pink to deep blue. A few clouds drift past, changing shape so slowly you can barely see them move. There's nothing you need to do. Just watch.

One cloud looks a little like a boat. Another like a sleeping animal. They drift, and soften, and dissolve into new shapes. You don't need to name them. You don't need to remember them. Just let them pass, the way thoughts pass, gently, without effort.
The air is warm and still. Somewhere far away, a bird sings a few final notes, then falls quiet. The grass beneath you is soft. The earth holds you completely. You feel heavy, safe and calm.

The first stars begin to appear. One, then another, then a few more. They arrive slowly, patiently, without any hurry at all. There's no need to count them. They'll be there all night, keeping quiet company with the sleeping world.
Let your breathing slow down to match the slow turning of the sky. Breathe in, gently. Breathe out, even more gently. Each breath a little softer than the last. Each moment a little quieter.
Nothing needs to happen. Nothing needs to be interesting. This stillness is not empty. It's full of rest, full of peace, full of the soft, quiet goodness of a night with nothing to do.
Your mind is calm. Your body is heavy. Your eyes are closed, or nearly closed. The stars are shining, the clouds are drifting, and you are drifting too. Slowly. Peacefully. Toward sleep.
Rest now. There's nowhere else to be. Just here, just now, just this gentle, quiet night.

Next time, we'll explore one of the most mysterious things your brain does every night. Dreaming. Why we dream, what dreams might be for, and why they're so strange. But that's for another night. For now, rest well. Goodnight.
